issues.description: The problem statement's UML and task text specify getTotalNumberOfStudents() should return an int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning a StudentCount object (and adds a new StudentCount class). This changes the method contract and introduces an extra type not present in the problem or template, which will confuse students about the expected return type and API to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem specification: change getTotalNumberOfStudents() in the solution to return an int (the sum of inscribed and guest students) instead of a StudentCount object, and remove the extra StudentCount class; or alternatively, update the problem statement and UML to explicitly introduce and document the StudentCount type and change the expected return type to StudentCount so all artifacts match.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify getTotalNumberOfStudents() returns an int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return a StudentCount object and introduces a StudentCount class. This introduces a new identifier/type for the same conceptual entity (the total number of students) that is not present in the problem or template and causes a signature/type mismatch, creating mapping confusion for students (they expect an int return value per the UML).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem/UML by changing getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return an int (sum of inscribed and guest students) and remove or avoid using the StudentCount wrapper class; or alternatively, update the problem statement and UML to explicitly introduce and document the StudentCount type as the intended return type. Preferably keep the return type as int to match the UML and reduce student confusion.
